name: teams
title: Teams (organizations, members, invitations)
description: Multi-tenancy for SaaS: teams with owner, admin, member and your own roles, email invitations (hashed single use tokens, expiry, resend, revoke), last owner protection and ownership transfer. Mark a resource team: true and its records stay inside their team in every route; 'member' and 'team:admin' work in any policy.
docs:
Teams: POST /api/teams { name } (you become owner), GET /api/teams, GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/teams/:teamId, GET /api/teams/:teamId/members, PATCH|DELETE /api/teams/:teamId/members/:userId, POST /api/teams/:teamId/leave, POST /api/teams/:teamId/transfer { userId }.
Invitations: POST /api/teams/:teamId/invitations { email, role } emails APP_URL/invite?token=... (option linkUrl); that page calls POST /api/teams/invitations/accept { token } signed in with the invited address. GET /api/teams/:teamId/invitations, DELETE .../invitations/:id, POST .../invitations/:id/resend.
Team-scoped data: resource('project', { team: true, fields, policy: { list: 'member', read: 'member', create: 'member', update: 'team:admin', delete: 'team:admin' } }). Clients pass team in the body or an X-Team header. Options (calm.config.js blocks.teams): roles, inviteRole, invitationTtlDays, verifiedEmailField, deleteRecords.

agents:
This project uses the teams block (app/blocks/teams/). Read app/blocks/teams/index.js (scoping, policies, routes) and teams.js (membership and invitation rules) before changing anything about tenancy.

Rules that must never break:
- Tenant isolation: a record of a team-scoped resource (team: true) is visible only to members of its team. Never bypass the service scope() for user-facing reads; { system: true } is for jobs and admin tooling only, with an explicit team filter.
- Never trust a team id from the body, query or X-Team header without checking membership. Use the policies ('member', 'team:admin', 'team:owner') or `(await app.ext.teams.memberships(ctx.user)).get(teamId)`.
- The team field is immutable: records never move between teams. Do not add a route that rewrites it.
- A team always has an owner: never demote or delete the last owner membership directly in MongoDB; use the block functions (changeRole, removeMember, transfer).
- Invitation tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and are single use. Never log, return or store a raw token.

Common tasks:
- Make a resource team-scoped: add `team: true` to resource(...) and use policies like list: 'member', create: 'member', update: 'team:admin'. Clients send `team` in the create body or an X-Team header.
- Team routes of your own: put :teamId in the path and use { policy: 'team:admin' }; the policy reads req.params.teamId.
- Seeds and scripts: app.ext.teams.create(user, { name }), app.ext.teams.addMember(teamId, userId, 'admin').
- New role: add it to blocks.teams.roles in calm.config.js (ordered, after 'owner' and 'admin'), then use 'team:<role>'.

Pitfalls: scope() needs the caller's memberships loaded by the block's guard, so service calls with another user than the request's must go through app.canRead() or { system: true }. The exposure matrix shows team rules as custom: write tests (two teams, a non-member, a removed member) for every team-scoped resource.
